dedupe_keys.name: gis multi criteria suitability screening for data centre siting in the united kingdom land 2026

description: This open-access study builds a GIS multi-criteria decision framework for regional suitability screening of data centre development in the United Kingdom. It excludes constrained zones such as protected areas and flood zones by binary masking, standardises climate indicators (temperature, air frost days, humidity, solar radiation) and infrastructure and environmental indicators (grid access, transport proximity, environmental protections, population distribution), weights them with the Analytic Hierarchy Process and combines them by weighted linear combination into a national suitability surface at 1 km resolution. Five candidate regions emerged, the Scottish Highlands, Northeast England, Southwest England (Cornwall), Northwest England and Eastern England, and a further comparison on power access, workforce, connectivity and hydro-climate constraints identified Lincolnshire as most suitable. Producer: five authors publishing in the MDPI journal Land on 23 March 2026. Coverage: the United Kingdom. Access: gold open access; the abstract, authors and licence were taken from the OpenAlex record because the publisher page refused the cloud session. Licence and cost: CC BY per OpenAlex, free to read. Caveats: a screening method whose weights are expert judgements, and the input layers and data licences were not read here. Simulation uses: the suitability surface and constraints support climate adaptation and siting studies for data centre capacity planning. Related record: CERF-DC, the data centre geospatial siting and cost package (model-cerf-dc-data-centre-geospatial-siting-costs).
